Microchip Technology.role: Microchip is a broad-based supplier of 8/16/32-bit microcontrollers and analog/mixed-signal chips for industrial, automotive and IoT; it sits in AI-infra as edge-compute silicon but is a cyclical embedded name emerging from a deep inventory-correction trough, so near-term recovery is real but demand

Skyworks Solutions.role: Skyworks makes RF front-end modules for smartphones and IoT/connectivity, with heavy customer concentration (notably Apple) making it a mature, cyclical handset-exposed name with flat revenue and only tangential AI-infra relevance.

Qorvo.role: Qorvo makes RF front-end modules concentrated in mobile handsets (heavy Apple/Android exposure) with modest connectivity and defense diversification; declining revenue, smartphone cyclicality, and tangential AI relevance place it as a mid-quality cyclical semiconductor name.

GlobalFoundries.role: GFS is a specialty semiconductor foundry focused on differentiated mature-node processes (RF, power, auto, IoT) rather than leading-edge AI logic, giving it stable but cyclical demand with modest growth and limited direct AI upside.

Intel.role: Legacy x86 CPU leader pivoting to foundry services and AI accelerators; execution risk, margin compression, and share loss to AMD/TSMC/Nvidia make the turnaround credible but unproven, hence mid-tier quality and elevated cyclicality.

Cirrus Logic.role: Cirrus supplies audio and mixed-signal components heavily concentrated in Apple smartphones; it sits as a cyclical, customer-concentrated mid-cap with modest AI exposure and flat-to-declining revenue tied to consumer handset demand rather than data-center AI buildout.

Allegro MicroSystems.role: Allegro designs magnetic position/current sensors and power ICs concentrated in automotive (EV/ADAS) and industrial markets; it sits as a cyclical semiconductor supplier with a solid niche moat but exposure to auto-production swings and inventory cycles, hence moderate quality and permanence.

Power Integrations.role: Power Integrations makes high-voltage power-conversion ICs for chargers, appliances and industrial systems with modest AI/data-center exposure; flat recent revenue and cyclical end-markets place it as a mid-quality, moderately cyclical semi name rather than a core AI beneficiary.

Wolfspeed.role: Vertically-integrated silicon-carbide wafer and device maker for EV/industrial power; heavy capex burn, negative earnings, balance-sheet distress and flat revenue make it a speculative, highly cyclical bet despite a credible SiC moat.

indie Semiconductor.role: Fabless designer of automotive ADAS and edge-sensing semiconductors (radar, LiDAR, connectivity); sits in disruptive with high beta and permanence due to pre-profitability, stalled recent revenue growth, small scale, and cyclical auto exposure despite a credible design-win backlog.

Navitas Semiconductor.role: Fabless GaN/SiC power-IC maker targeting datacenter power delivery; tiny revenue base, currently shrinking YoY and unprofitable, with credible but unproven datacenter design-win pipeline, hence speculative disruptive classification with high permanence risk.

FormFactor.role: FormFactor makes advanced probe cards and test systems used to validate semiconductors including HBM and logic; it holds a leading share in a consolidated but cyclical test market tied to fab and packaging capex, giving it durable but capex-sensitive demand.

Cohu.role: Cohu supplies test handlers, contactors and consumables for semiconductor back-end testing; it sits in AI-infra but is cyclical and mid-moat, exposed to chip capex swings with modest recurring consumables revenue.

Advanced Energy Industries.role: Supplies precision power conversion and RF systems used in semiconductor fabrication and data-center equipment; sits as a cyclical AI-infra picks-and-shovels supplier levered to fab capex, with a solid but not dominant niche and meaningful exposure to equipment spending cycles.

Entegris.role: Entegris supplies ultra-high-purity materials, filtration and specialty chemicals consumed in semiconductor fabrication; much revenue is recurring/consumable-driven (softening cyclicality) but still tied to fab utilization and wafer starts, so it sits as a credible-but-cyclical AI-infra enabler with

MKS Instruments.role: MKS supplies critical subsystems (vacuum, photonics, RF power, materials/plating) into semiconductor and electronics manufacturing; it benefits from AI-driven fab investment but remains cyclical and carries meaningful debt from the Atotech acquisition, hence moderate quality and elevated cyclicality

Photronics.role: Photronics is a leading independent maker of photomasks used in chip and display fabrication; it sits in cyclical semiconductor supply with modest growth, decent share as a merchant supplier, but exposure to foundry capex cycles and flat recent revenue.

Veeco Instruments.role: Veeco supplies specialized deposition, ion-beam, and thermal processing equipment used in advanced logic, memory, and compound-semiconductor fabs; it is a niche AI-infra hardware play with meaningful but cyclical exposure and modest market share versus larger equipment peers.

Axcelis Technologies.role: Axcelis makes ion implantation systems for semiconductor fabrication, heavily weighted to mature-node power/automotive (SiC) chips; it sits in AI-infra as a cyclical WFE supplier with modest AI exposure, currently facing flat revenue amid a power-chip inventory correction, giving it moderate moat bu

Ultra Clean Holdings.role: Contract manufacturer of fluid-delivery and gas-handling subsystems for wafer-fab equipment OEMs; it sits in AI-infra as a cyclical, capex-dependent supplier with thin margins and limited pricing power, leaving it highly exposed to fab spending swings.

Vishay Intertechnology.role: Broad-line maker of discrete semiconductors and passive components (resistors, capacitors, inductors) with modest AI/data-center exposure; sits as a cyclical, fragmented commodity supplier with thin secular tailwinds and cyclical end-market demand.

Littelfuse.role: Littelfuse makes fuses, circuit protection and power semiconductor components for industrial, automotive and electronics markets; it is a diversified cyclical component supplier with only tangential AI/datacenter exposure, so it sits as a moderate-quality defensive/cyclical name with modest single-d

TE Connectivity.role: Diversified connector and sensor maker whose AI-relevant datacenter/high-speed interconnect segment is a growing minority of ~$19.3bn total revenue; solid moat but cyclical industrial exposure caps AI-specific upside.

Flex.role: Flex is a diversified electronics manufacturing services provider whose data-center/power infrastructure segment benefits from AI buildout, but thin EMS margins, fragmented competition, and cyclical capex exposure keep it a mid-quality infra proxy rather than a pure AI winner.

Sanmina peer / Benchmark.role: Benchmark is a diversified EMS provider serving aerospace/defense, medical, industrial, and semiconductor-capital-equipment customers; it sits in AI-infra only tangentially, with thin margins, low moat, and cyclical demand that limit both growth and earnings durability.

Digital Realty Trust.role: Global data center REIT leasing colocation and interconnection capacity that benefits from AI-driven compute demand; recurring lease revenue makes it defensive-leaning infra, but modest top-line growth and REIT valuation temper AI upside.

Equinix.role: Leading neutral colocation and interconnection REIT whose recurring, contract-based revenue and dense ecosystem moat provide durable demand, though growth is steady rather than explosive and capital intensity caps upside.

Eaton.role: Diversified electrical equipment maker whose datacenter power distribution, switchgear and UPS segment benefits from AI buildout; sits in AI-infra with solid but partly cyclical earnings tied to construction capex.

GE Vernova.role: GE Vernova supplies gas turbines, grid equipment, and electrification hardware benefiting from data-center power demand and grid buildout; it sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels beneficiary but with cyclical, capex-driven revenue and modest organic growth.

Quanta Services.role: Leading specialty contractor building and maintaining electric transmission, distribution, and grid infrastructure benefiting from data-center power demand and electrification; sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels beneficiary but revenue growth is steady rather than explosive and demand carries s

Emerson Electric.role: Diversified industrial automation supplier with process controls, software, and instrumentation exposed to data-center and reshoring capex; sits in defensive due to entrenched installed base and recurring aftermarket, but revenue is cyclical and tied to industrial/plant capex cycles.

Schneider peer / Hubbell.role: Hubbell makes electrical and utility grid infrastructure (transmission/distribution components, metering, connectors); it benefits from grid modernization and data-center power buildout, but is a mature, cyclical industrial with modest single-digit growth rather than an AI pure-play.

Powell Industries.role: Powell makes switchgear, bus duct and electrical distribution systems for datacenters, utilities and oil/gas; it's a real beneficiary of AI power buildout but remains a cyclical, project-driven industrial with modest reported YoY growth and exposure to capex swings.

Oklo.role: Pre-revenue developer of small fast-spectrum nuclear reactors targeting data-center and industrial power; speculative given no operating plants, no NRC-approved deployment yet, and revenue years away despite strong AI-power narrative.

Uranium / Ur-Energy.role: Small US-based in-situ uranium miner leveraged to nuclear fuel demand and utility contracting; a tiny-revenue, commodity-price-driven single name with a small share of a cyclical market, hence speculative positioning and elevated terminal risk.

GE Aerospace peer / Chart.role: Chart makes cryogenic and process-cooling equipment for industrial gas, LNG and increasingly data-center thermal management, giving it modest AI-adjacent exposure but a cyclical, capex-driven core with fragmented competition and a flat recent revenue trend.

Twilio.role: Twilio provides programmable messaging/voice CPaaS APIs and is layering AI (Segment data, contextual comms) atop a usage-based model; solid recurring revenue but modest ~4% growth, competitive pressure, and pricing sensitivity temper its AI-platform positioning.

Okta.role: Okta provides cloud identity and access management (SSO, MFA, IGA) via a recurring SaaS model; sticky but facing intense competition from Microsoft Entra and decelerating growth, placing it as a defensive-to-mid-quality software name.

Docusign.role: Docusign leads e-signature and is extending into AI-driven agreement management (IAM), but core growth has decelerated to low single digits and the AI layer is early monetization; sits as a mature, recurring-revenue software name with moderate moat and modest AI upside.

UiPath.role: UiPath is a leading robotic process automation platform pivoting toward agentic AI, but decelerating ~4% YoY growth and stiff competition from Microsoft and ServiceNow cap its moat and place it mid-tier with elevated single-name risk.

Pegasystems.role: Enterprise BPM/CRM software vendor pivoting to AI-driven decisioning and workflow automation; flat-to-slightly-negative revenue and mid-tier moat place it as a modest AI-platform play with recurring subscription revenue but real competition from larger platforms.

Fastly.role: Fastly runs an edge cloud/CDN platform competing with larger players like Cloudflare and Akamai; slowing ~5% growth, thin moat, and persistent unprofitability place it as a speculative, competitively pressured name.

Amdocs.role: Amdocs provides mission-critical BSS/OSS billing and customer-experience software to global telecom carriers, with sticky multi-year contracts and recurring revenue; it sits as a low-beta defensive with modest but durable growth, where AI is an incremental upsell to a mature, slow-growth core rather

Verint Systems.role: Verint sells customer-experience and workforce-engagement software with AI-driven analytics; flat revenue, modest moat, and a crowded CX/contact-center market place it as a low-multiple defensive name with muted AI upside.

BigBear.ai.role: Small-cap provider of AI-driven decision analytics for defense and government customers; flat revenue, persistent losses, dilution risk, and a fragmented competitive field against primes and larger software vendors place it in the speculative tier despite a credible government-anchored TAM.

Rigetti Computing.role: Rigetti builds superconducting quantum processors and cloud access but generates negligible revenue against ongoing cash burn, making it a speculative pre-commercial bet on an unproven market where technical and competitive risks make deep drawdowns potentially terminal.

D-Wave Quantum.role: D-Wave sells quantum-annealing systems and cloud access targeting optimization workloads, but with ~$10M revenue that fell ~49% YoY, no profits, and unproven commercial demand, it is a highly speculative bet whose deep drawdowns carry meaningful terminal risk.
